changes: p2 roles: dropped 'commissioner' because the verb is 'likhitam' (written), not 'likhāpitam'. The instrumental agent ('…vāsinā … puṇyārthinā … likhitam') is the writer. Read Vajābhāvoka as that agent (genitive -kasya for instrumental -kena), giving roles scribe + beneficiary ('pūjārthaṃ'). Confidence lowered to low.
p2 residence normalised to 'Hallapiṅga viṣaya, Kāthadhuṭollaka' (kāpicāsinā read as -ka-vāsinā).
p1 confidence lowered to low: no king 'Mandaratha' is known for Nepal c. 1092 (Harṣadeva or Śivadeva). He may be a local ruler of Hallapiṅga, or the name may be corrupt.
date.weekday given as 'Friday (śukradine)'; nakṣatra normalised to Aśvinī.

purpose: pūjārtha, puṇyārtha (for Vajābhāvoka's worship and merit)
notes: 'rāja' probably stands for 'rājye' (under the reign of). No king named 'Mandaratha' is known in Nepal around NS 212 (1092 CE), when Harṣadeva or Śivadeva ruled. He may be a local ruler of the Hallapiṅga viṣaya, or the name may be corrupt (e.g. for 'śrīmad-…'). 'kāthadhuṭōllakāpicāsinā' is probably an error for 'kāthadhuṭollaka-vāsinā' (resident of Kāthadhuṭollaka). The colophon has an instrumental agent ('…vāsinā … puṇyārthinā … [li]khitam') alongside the genitive 'kulaputravajābhāvokasya pūjārtha[ṃ]'. There are two readings: (a) the genitive is a case error for the instrumental, so Vajābhāvoka is the scribe and wrote the copy for his own worship (adopted here); (b) the writer is unnamed and Vajābhāvoka is only the beneficiary. Nothing supports 'commissioner', since the verb is likhitam, not likhāpitam. 'khitam(!)' = likhitam. The name may be a corruption of 'Vajrābhāvoka' or similar. The tithi is not stated.
